capabilities: Arrange modules as resizable cards on a tiled page
Create and switch workspace pages with their own cards and background
Show daily notes, tasks, agenda, calendar and vault files
Run a shell, web page, music and podcasts inside cards
Record dictation and spoken commands on macOS
extras: Ten of the 21 modules are marked with a dot and need an Atrium Complete license; a 30-day trial starts from Settings → Atrium. Terminal, Calendar events and Dictation run other programs through Node's child_process on desktop only, and Atrium checks with /bin/sh which programs exist. On macOS the atrium-calendar and atrium-speech Swift helpers are downloaded once per version from GitHub releases into the plugin folder and marked executable with chmod. Per-module settings and keys are in a separate online guide at atrium-md.com.
problem: Obsidian opens on a file or an empty note with no home view, so a dashboard of notes, tasks and tools has to be assembled from several plugins.

relations.evidence: A spoken command can ask Claude Code, in a terminal card, if you turn that on.
Atrium reads events from icalBuddy if you have it installed.
read and edit the Calendar app's events through atrium-calendar

summary: Homepage plugin that tiles resizable cards, each a module such as daily note, tasks, agenda, clock or terminal, over your existing notes.
